evidence.support_text: In a ‘split adjuvant’ test with 20 treated and 20 control Hartley guinea pigs, TCS (10% in Vaseline) was applied to epilated skin three times. Complete Freund’s adjuvant was administered intradermally between the second and third induction doses. After 13 days, 3% TCS (in petrolatum) was used in the occluded patch test for 24 hr and skin sensitization was measured at 24, 48 and 72 hr. After challenge, 7 out of the 20 test animals showed some erythema without edema and vesicle formation, which resolved after 1 or 2 days. In a stimulation test, erythema was observed in one out of 20 animals, and this erythema did not resolve at 72 hr, but no edema was observed. Since no response was seen in the control group, it was concluded that TCS had a very low skin sensitization index (3,35,62). Table 5 summarizes skin sensitization in response to TCS.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 0.1 ml of 10% cis-jasmone in propylene glycol, occluded, 10 applications on alternate days for 3 weeks; challenge: same concentration; 11 Hartley albino guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: In a modified Buehler sensitization test, 11 Hartley albino guinea pigs received topical induction applications of 0.1 ml of 10% cis-jasmone in propylene glycol under occlusion; after a rest period, challenge at the same concentration gave no reaction in any animal (RIFM, 1971c).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 5% in petrolatum, 6 h, once per week for 3 weeks; Pirbright guinea pigs (n=20); challenge after 2 weeks; score at 24 and 48 h post-patch removal
evidence.support_text: In a modified Buehler sensitization test, 20 Pirbright guinea pigs received an induction application of 5% 1,3-dimethyl-3-phenylbutyl acetate in petrolatum for 6 h once per week for 3 weeks. Two weeks after the final induction application, a challenge dose was administered. There was no primary skin irritation in comparison to the control animals.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 0.1 ml of 10% 2-hexylidene cyclopentanone in propylene glycol, topical, alternate days for 3 weeks under occlusion; challenge: same concentration; albino Hartley guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: In a modified Buehler test with 10% 2-hexylidene cyclopentanone in propylene glycol for induction and challenge, there was no reaction in any of the 11 guinea pigs.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 0.3 ml of 1% 2-hexylidene cyclopentanone in 80% ethanol/20% distilled water, topical, 6 h/week for 3 weeks; challenge: 0.5%, 1.5%, and 5% in DEP, 6 h; albino Hartley guinea pigs; scores at 24 and 48 h
evidence.support_text: In a modified Buehler test with 1% 2-hexylidene cyclopentanone in 80% ethanol/20% distilled water for induction and challenge concentrations of 0.5%, 1.5%, and 5% in DEP, slight erythema was seen at all doses at an incidence higher than controls, suggesting sensitization had occurred.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 0.3 ml of 2.5% 2-hexylidene cyclopentanone in 80% ethanol/20% distilled water, topical, 6 h/week for 3 weeks; challenge: 2.5% in acetone, 6 h; albino Hartley guinea pigs; scores at 24 and 48 h
evidence.support_text: In a modified Buehler test with 2.5% 2-hexylidene cyclopentanone in 80% ethanol/20% distilled water for induction and a challenge of 2.5% in acetone, slight or moderate patchy erythema was seen in 9/20 guinea pigs compared to no incidence in controls, suggesting sensitization.

review_policy.eligible_subject: unique measurement-producing subject, donor, or cell-system species
